newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jailed ex-Cannes mayor locked in new sleaze probe.
newsitem.headline: Jailed ex-Cannes mayor locked in new sleaze probe.

text.p: The jailed former mayor of the French Riviera resort of Cannes, Michel Mouillot, was escorted from his cell on Tuesday and placed under police surveillance with his wife in a new corruption probe.

Police and justice sources said Mouillot, jailed since July in a separate sleaze probe, was suspected of illicitly receiving funds through an employee of a subsidiary of water utility Compagnie Generale des Eaux.

Investigators said the funds -- more than 10 million francs ($1.7 million) -- were channeled to Mouillot through the Phenix real estate firm, which at the time was headed by a Mouillot associate, Jean Marc Oury.

The employee, Oury's former secretary Micheline Clerq who now works for the chairman of Compagnie Generale, was placed under investigation for alleged corruption on Tuesday and ordered held in custody in Nice by investigating magistrate Philippe Alenda.

The investigation started when co-owners of part of the Croisette seafront boulevard appealed to magistrates in a tussle with the town hall which wanted to expropriate them to build a hotel complex close to the Palm Beach casino.
The plaintiffs accused Mouillot of "distorting a public procedure for the benefit of private interests".
Mouillot resigned in February after the Supreme Court threw out an appeal against his previous conviction for sleaze.

Once dubbed the "Kennedy of the Croisette", the centre-right politician was barred from holding public office for five years as part of an 18-month suspended prison sentence and 200,000 franc ($40,000) fine for receiving a ficticious salary from a Lyon businessman.
He has been in pre-trial custody since last July for two other corruption cases in which he is accused of having solicited bribes in exchange for permits to install one-arm bandits in casinos.
